notes: rl2:anyAgent as subject → no assignee on the permission, so the party part is absent from the applies predicate and any requester matches. The agent-scoped fact agent.ethicsApprovalValid becomes one state property, ex:requesterEthicsApprovalValid; the SOTW is assembled for one request and its flattened properties describe that request's subject (due2-workflows.md §3.3). RL2's board attribution and validity interval are an admissibility filter (config admit_source / admit_age), and a value that fails it arrives as missing. RL2's 'absent-but-defaulted' value has no due2 counterpart (due2 has no operand defaults); the assembler must supply the false value, so scenario 2 uses a resolved false. Scenario 4 is added: a request that names no subject gives the assembler no one to resolve a subject-scoped fact for, so the fact is missing and the verdict Indeterminate.

expected.why: The permission has no assignee, action and target match, and the approval fact is true, so it applies; it has no duties.
false = true is F, so the permission does not apply; nothing else applies.
Missing gives U for the constraint and the permission: Permit in the permissive completion, NotApplicable in the restrictive one.

The permission has no atom_party, so the missing subject is not itself a U part; but the subject-scoped approval fact has no subject to describe (§3.3) and is missing, so the constraint and the permission are U and the completions disagree.
